name: _test_functorch_fallback
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_test_functorch_fallback(Tensor self, Tensor other) -> Tensor. Registered signatures: aten::_test_functorch_fallback(Tensor self, Tensor other) -> Tensor ; aten::_test_functorch_fallback.out(Tensor self, Tensor other, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract for both overloads, including keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation; do not narrow tests to this representative signature. Semantics derived from the tests: returns a fresh, non-view copy of self; a new storage pointer is asserted for non-empty input, and the alias check is made against self only, not against other. other is never read, so its shape and dtype cannot affect the result. A dense self keeps its strides in the result while stepped/offset/expanded self is materialized and the lazy conjugate bit is dropped. The test module reports CPU and Meta as the only native kernels and CUDA operands as raising NotImplementedError; the supplied cases run CPU tensors only. There is no autograd formula, so torch.autograd.grad raises RuntimeError('derivative for aten::_test_functorch_fallback is not implemented'). The out overload takes a keyword-only Tensor(a!) out buffer, mutates it and returns that same buffer by identity, writing through the caller's layout (strides and storage offset) and resizing a too-small buffer to the input shape; in the tested float32-input/float64-out-buffer case the call raises (RuntimeError or TypeError).
